chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar, from his father, from his grandfather Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Khalid al-Qalanisi, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'One prayer in the mosque of Kufa is equivalent to a thousand prayers.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.بِأَلْفِ صَلَاةٍ: Equivalent to a thousand prayers, indicating multiplied reward
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الْكُوفَةِ: The mosque of Kufa, a significant religious site in Iraq

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying in the mosque of Kufa according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscores the spiritual merit of the Kufa Mosque, a site deeply associated with Imam Ali (AS) and the early Imams, thereby elevating its status as a primary center of Shia worship. The reward of 'one thousand prayers' reflects the broader Shia tradition of *fadail al-a'mal* (virtues of deeds), where specific locations and times amplify the value of acts of devotion. This emphasis aligns with the Quranic principle that sanctified spaces, like the Kaaba or the Prophet's Mosque, hold unique spiritual gravity for believers.
